questions.question: When a request arrives, how does the app decide which handler gets it, and what happens if no path matches?
questions.answerNote: Router::call_with_state asks PathRouter, which looks the URI path up in a matchit::Router (Node) to get a RouteId, stores MatchedPath and URL params in request extensions, then calls the endpoint's MethodRouter (which picks by HTTP method). On MatchError::NotFound the request goes to the catch_all_fallback, which defaults to the NotFound service (404).

questions.question: If a client posts a JSON body that is malformed or has the wrong fields, what status code do they get and where is that decided?
questions.answerNote: The Json extractor first checks Content-Type is application/json (or +json) else MissingJsonContentType -> 415. It buffers the body and deserializes with serde_path_to_error: syntax/EOF errors -> JsonSyntaxError 400; valid JSON of the wrong shape (Category::Data) -> JsonDataError 422. Statuses and bodies are declared with define_rejection! in extract/rejection.rs.

questions.question: Is there a cap on how large a request body can be, and how do I raise or remove it?
questions.answerNote: Body-consuming extractors built on Bytes (String, Json, Form...) are limited to 2 MB by default: with_limited_body wraps the body in http_body_util::Limited with DEFAULT_LIMIT = 2_097_152 unless a DefaultBodyLimit layer set another value. Use .layer(DefaultBodyLimit::max(n)) or DefaultBodyLimit::disable(); this is local to extractors, unlike tower-http's RequestBodyLimit which applies globally.
questions.labelFix: Post-freeze mechanical fix (CLA-289 review): '2 ?MB' was regex syntax that the literal matcher could never satisfy; now '2 MB' (with '2mb' / '2_097_152' alternatives). Question and expected files unchanged.

questions.question: What's the recommended way to give every request handler access to a database connection pool?
questions.answerNote: Put it in an app-state struct (derive Clone, often wrap in Arc), attach with Router::with_state(state), and take State<AppState> as a handler argument (before any body extractor). Substates can be pulled out via FromRef. Alternatives documented in lib.rs 'Sharing state with handlers': Extension layer or closure captures; request-derived data belongs in Extension, not State.

questions.question: The compiler says my async function can't be used as a route handler because some trait isn't implemented. What are the rules, and how do I get a clearer error?
questions.answerNote: A handler must be an async fn with <=16 arguments, all but the last implementing FromRequestParts and the last FromRequest, returning IntoResponse, and its future must be Send (don't hold !Send across .await). Rust's error is opaque; annotate the function with #[axum_macros::debug_handler] (axum-macros) to get a targeted diagnostic.

questions.question: If I stack several middleware layers on a router, in what order do they see the request?
questions.answerNote: Each Router::layer call wraps everything added before it, so with .layer(a).layer(b).layer(c) the request passes c -> b -> a -> handler and the response returns a -> b -> c (bottom to top, onion model). Layers composed inside a tower::ServiceBuilder run top to bottom, which is why ServiceBuilder is recommended.

questions.question: How do I make the server finish in-flight requests and stop cleanly when I hit Ctrl-C?
questions.answerNote: axum::serve(listener, app).with_graceful_shutdown(signal_future). When the future resolves the accept loop stops taking new connections, each connection is told to shut down gracefully via a watch channel, and serve waits for all connection tasks to finish. The example builds the signal from tokio::signal::ctrl_c and SIGTERM and adds a TimeoutLayer so slow requests cannot block shutdown forever.

questions.question: Where is the support for cookies that the client can read but can't tamper with?
questions.answerNote: axum-extra's SignedCookieJar (cookie/signed.rs, 'cookie-signed' feature) signs and verifies cookies with a cookie::Key obtained via FromRef from state; values remain readable plaintext (use PrivateCookieJar in cookie/private.rs for encryption). The modified jar must be returned from the handler for Set-Cookie headers to be sent.
